checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.why: Clip is stated as 10 s and frames up to 9.5 s were extracted.

must.item: One continuous excerpt from source with source framing and speed preserved
must.why: Re-rendered at 832x512 (about 1.63:1) instead of 16:9. The frames show different shots and cockpit views, and the source frame shows a burned-in caption bar. Fidelity to the source is doubtful.

must.item: Excerpt contains salient jet action or cockpit interaction
must.why: Shows jets flying over the sea and pilots in the cockpit exchanging dialogue.

must.item: Original sound synchronized, no replacement music/narration/captions added
must.why: The clip has sound, but I can't verify that it matches the source. Subtitles are burned in ('Rook, you with me?', 'Right here, Vega.'), and they may be original or AI-generated.

faults.what: Output is an AI re-render at 832x512 with a changed aspect ratio, low-res softness and some AI artefacts (smeared sky and cloud shapes, slightly warped cockpit details).
Burned-in subtitles appear in the output. They may not be from the original, and the user did not ask for captions.
The excerpt was picked blindly as the middle 10 s. It is not clearly the best part.

summary: The result is a 10-second AI re-render of seconds 10–20 at 832×512. It has jet and cockpit action, but it is not a faithful cut: the aspect ratio changed, there are AI artefacts, and subtitles appear, so it falls short of a true trim.
